claims.note: Sender: 'We estimate the total number of bacteria in the 70 kg "reference man" to be 3.8·10^13 ... revise past estimates to 3.0·10^13 human cells'; 30/68 = 44%. B/H '1.3, with an uncertainty of 25%' gives ~38-51% human. Hatton: '≈36 trillion cells in the male' (70 kg); 36/(36+38) = 49%. 'About half' is within A3. 'Typical man' = the 70 kg reference man; Sender's author summary: 'the typical adult human body consists of about 30 trillion human cells and about 38 trillion bacteria'. 'Best' is evaluative framing: these are the two most recent whole-body counts, and Hatton calls the earlier studies 'converging on values of 30 to 37 trillion human cells'.
